summary: No trans-related provincial statute, enforcement series or incident pattern specific to La Rioja was documented in the country dossier — but "no signal" there means "no documentation", not "no exposure": like every Argentine province it retains contravención/faltas police codes identified by an NGO survey as the instrument behind most arrests of trans and travesti people, and, like other interior provinces, it has neither a visible community presence nor reporting infrastructure to generate records. The February 2025 national decrees curtailing the Gender Identity Law — banning gender-transition hormone and surgical treatment for minors and changing prison placement of trans people — apply here as in all provinces, against a deteriorating national picture (a record 227 anti-LGBT hate crimes in 2025, up 62% year-on-year).

Agencia Presentes report (19 March 2026) on the Observatorio Nacional de Crímenes de Odio's 2025 tally: at least 227 hate crimes against people for sexual orientation or gender identity, up 62% year-on-year and the highest figure of the observatory's ten years of operation — one every 38 hours; perpetrators were predominantly security-force personnel and unidentified attackers in public space, beating the main modality, in a context the observatory attributes to the national government's "cultural battle" against LGBTI+ people; attacks continued in early 2026, including a life-endangering home invasion of an LGBTIQ+ organisation president in Jujuy.
